name: basically-vscode
description: Language support for retro BASIC — problems, completion, hover, jump-to-definition, outline and colour, for the machine each listing is written for.

commands.title: Choose the machine to check against

basically.machine.markdownDescription: The machine every listing is checked against, by its id or its full name (`zx81`, `BBC Micro`). A listing that declares its own machine with a `#MACHINE` line ignores this, so one project can hold programs for several machines. Left empty, the machine is worked out from the listing where that is possible, and reported as a problem where it is not. Run **Basically: Choose the machine to check against** to pick from the machines this server has.

basically.server.path.markdownDescription: Path to the `basically` command, or to a checkout's `cli.mjs`, to serve from instead of the copy bundled with this extension. For working on the toolchain itself.

basically.server.nodePath.markdownDescription: Path to the Node.js used to run the bundled server. Left empty, `node` from your PATH is used where it is new enough, and the editor's own Node otherwise.

basically.trace.server.description: Trace the conversation between VS Code and the language server, in the Basically output channel.

scripts.prepackage: node ../../scripts/fetch-server.mjs && npm run compile && node -e "require('node:fs').mkdirSync('../../dist', { recursive: true })"
